checks.label: Replication
checks.explain: Replication threads on this server: the receiver (IO thread) that copies the source's binary log and the applier (SQL thread) that runs it. Read with SHOW SLAVE STATUS; nothing is started or stopped.
checks.why: 1 replication channel; default channel: receiver Yes, applier No; applier error 1062: Could not execute Write_rows event on table review.repl_probe; Duplicate entry '7' for key 'PRIMARY', Error_code: 1062; handler error HA_ERR_FOUND_DUPP_KEY; the event's master log mysql-bin.000003, end_log_pos 15938341; lag unknown (NULL). Rule of thumb: problem when a replication thread is stopped or reports an error; watch while the receiver is still connecting, or when the lag reaches 60 s; problem at 600 s.
checks.rule: problem when a replication thread is stopped or reports an error; watch while the receiver is still connecting, or when the lag reaches 60 s; problem at 600 s
checks.caveat: Seconds_Behind_Master is NULL while the applier is stopped and while the receiver is not connected (on MySQL once the applier has caught up), 0 when the applier caught up with what the receiver has (even when the receiver is behind the source), and skewed by a clock change on either server, so a 0 is not proof that the replica is current.

action.text: Read the error and the applier state in the Replication view or with SHOW SLAVE STATUS; fix the cause before restarting a thread. Skipping a failed transaction leaves this replica different from its source.

checks.label: Writable replica
checks.explain: Writes made on a replica are not on its source; they make the replica differ and can stop replication when the source later changes the same rows.
checks.why: This server is a replica and read_only is OFF, so any user can write to it. Rule of thumb: watch when a replica accepts writes (read_only=OFF).
checks.rule: watch when a replica accepts writes (read_only=OFF)
checks.caveat: Some setups write to a replica on purpose (a reporting schema, a multi-source aggregator). read_only=ON still lets users with SUPER write; super_read_only=ON stops them too.

action.text: Make the replica read-only unless writes are intended; the setting is global and needs the db-operations confirmation.

checks.why: No unlocked account has an empty password. Rule of thumb: problem when an unlocked account with a password plugin has an empty authentication string.
checks.rule: problem when an unlocked account with a password plugin has an empty authentication string
checks.caveat: Find the applications that use the account first: a new password or a lock breaks their logins.

checks.label: root from any host
checks.explain: Account basics from mysql.user: accounts that accept a login without a password, anonymous accounts, and root allowed from any host. Only account names are read; password hashes never leave the server.
checks.why: 'root'@'%' exists and is not locked: the most privileged account accepts logins from every host, so only its password protects it. Rule of thumb: watch when 'root'@'%' exists and is not locked.
checks.rule: watch when 'root'@'%' exists and is not locked

action.text: Limit root to the hosts that administer the server; each statement needs the db-operations confirmation.

checks.label: Query cache
checks.explain: The query cache keeps the result of a SELECT and returns it for the same statement text. Every lookup and every invalidation takes one global mutex, and any change to a table drops every cached result that read it.
checks.why: Off (query_cache_type=OFF, query_cache_size=1,048,576). Rule of thumb: ok when off; watch when on (query_cache_type ON or DEMAND with query_cache_size above 0).
checks.rule: ok when off; watch when on (query_cache_type ON or DEMAND with query_cache_size above 0)

checks.label: Binary log expiry
checks.explain: Binary logs are kept until they expire or someone purges them; expiry runs at startup and when the server rotates to a new binary log.
checks.why: The binary log is on and does not expire (expire_logs_days is 0), so it grows until the disk fills unless something purges it. Rule of thumb: watch when the binary log is on and nothing purges it automatically (no expiry period and no total size limit).
checks.rule: watch when the binary log is on and nothing purges it automatically (no expiry period and no total size limit)
checks.caveat: Replicas and point-in-time recovery need the binary logs since their last position or backup: keep them longer than a replica may be down and longer than your backup interval. A job that runs PURGE BINARY LOGS also counts.

action.text: Set an expiry in whole days that covers your replicas and backups; the setting is global and needs the db-operations confirmation. MySQL 5.7 has no SET PERSIST, so also add the line to the option file.

checks.label: Total memory budget
checks.why: Computed configured global capacities plus per-connection scenario times each connection count; physical RAM is unknown over SQL (never inferred from buffer settings)
checks.rule: unknown without physical RAM or complete inputs; watch when the modeled connection budget exceeds RAM; problem when configured global capacities alone exceed RAM
checks.caveat: Both net_buffer_length buffers (network and result) are allocated at connect; thread_stack at thread creation. Other session buffers are allocated on demand, some per table or per join. Both binlog caches are created together on a session's first binlog write; this scenario counts binlog_cache_size and binlog_stmt_cache_size only with log_bin ON; unknown logging leaves a partial subtotal. MariaDB counts two redo buffers of innodb_log_buffer_size; memory-mapped redo can bypass these allocations. The scenario can overstate use when sessions do not need all buffers together. It uses one sort/join/read buffer per connection and one MEMORY temporary table, not a hard upper bound: joins and queries can allocate several buffers/tables; network buffers grow. TempTable thread-local blocks, allocator overhead, other engines, the OS, other processes and container limits are not included; mmap limits are file-backed capacity, not added as RAM. P_S includes only its own internal buffers to avoid double counting other buffers. Global defaults may differ from existing session settings; a peak connection count is not measured peak memory. A budget below RAM does not establish safety.

action.text: Compare with server/container memory and measured peak use before changing limits.

numbers.label: One internal MEMORY table per connection

checks.rule: problem from the listed end of maintenance; watch within 180 days before it; unknown for an unlisted series or an unproved end date
checks.caveat: Static series-level maintenance dates, not a check of installed patches or vulnerabilities. MySQL dates include Extended Support, exclude Sustaining Support; MariaDB dates describe Community binary maintenance, not Enterprise contracts. Current means the reviewed current LTS line, not the latest patch or Innovation release. Fork/distributor support can differ. Listed end dates come from vendor policy/release pages, not server source or tag timestamps. Month-only dates use the first day after the final maintenance month. Verify vendor policy before scheduling an upgrade; this table can become stale.

action.text: Check the vendor lifecycle and test an upgrade to a maintained series.
